source_text: Pax in terra; quinque centum persequentur. Pax Christi; pauci fortes terga hostium.
thought_title: Peace and the few who rout many
orientation: Origen is expounding the blessings promised in Leviticus 26 to those who walk in God's precepts, interpreting them spiritually.
pass_a_gloss: Peace on earth; five hundred [people] will pursue. [The] peace of Christ; [the] few strong [ones] [will see] [the] backs of [the] enemies.

choices.why: Keeps the simple noun phrase and the spatial sense of 'in terra' as the sphere where peace is given.
rejected: There will be peace on the earth

choices.why: Preserves the abrupt numeric subject and the future tense of the verb, matching the promise form of Leviticus 26:8.
rejected: a hundred will be pursued by five

choices.why: Renders the genitive as possessive, marking the shift from earthly peace to the specifically Christian peace.

choices.english: a few strong men the backs of enemies
choices.why: Keeps the elliptical construction without a verb, preserving the terse antithesis with the preceding clause.
rejected: a few strong men will turn the backs of enemies
few brave men rout the enemy

bible_refs.note: Pax in terra; quinque centum persequentur

pass_b_english: Peace on earth; five hundred will pursue. The peace of Christ; a few strong men the backs of enemies.

last_rejected.quote: a few strong men the backs of enemies
last_rejected.why: Missing verb; English is ungrammatical and incomprehensible.
last_rejected.fix: a few strong men will turn the backs of enemies.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'pauci fortes terga hostium' also lacks a verb; elliptical phrase matches source. Not a translation error.
